cards.a: ERSPAN mirrors traffic across a routed/IP network by encapsulating mirrored packets in IP/GRE toward a destination on any reachable subnet, extending SPAN beyond a single switch.

The mirrored frame is wrapped with GRE and an outer IP header: the outer IP provides router-to-router routing, GRE tunnels to the destination, and the original mirrored frame is carried as the payload; the result is routable.

cards.q: How do SPAN, RSPAN, and ERSPAN differ?
cards.a: SPAN is local, RSPAN is remote via a Layer 2 VLAN, and ERSPAN is remote via Layer 3 IP/GRE routing.

cards.q: What commands configure an ERSPAN source session?
cards.a: Use monitor session N type erspan-source, then monitor session N source interface Gi x/y (both), and under monitor session N destination set erspan id 100, erspan ip-address, and erspan origin-ip.

cards.q: What fields are required in the ERSPAN destination configuration?
cards.a: The destination needs erspan id (session key), erspan ip-address (remote destination), and erspan origin-ip (source IP).

cards.q: What are the requirements for ERSPAN to work?
cards.a: Both routers need IP routes plus GRE support, the ACL must permit GRE, and MTU headroom must account for GRE overhead.

cards.q: What are the caveats of ERSPAN?
cards.a: MTU may need raising or fragmenting, there is extra CPU processing, overload must be planned for traffic rate, and only IP is carried (no raw Layer 2).

cards.q: What is the GRE overhead of ERSPAN?
cards.a: ERSPAN adds roughly 50 bytes of GRE/IP overhead, so MTU size matters.

cards.q: Nothing is received at the ERSPAN destination; what is the likely cause and check?
cards.a: Likely a routing problem; check by pinging the destination. Also verify origin IP with show monitor, MTU for fragmentation, ACL permitting GRE, and matching erspan id on both sides.

cards.q: Which session type command is used for ERSPAN source side?
cards.a: monitor session N type erspan-source (with an erspan-destination type on the receiver side).

cards.q: What is the difference between RSPAN and ERSPAN?
cards.a: RSPAN is remote Layer 2 mirroring over a VLAN, while ERSPAN is remote Layer 3 routed mirroring over IP/GRE.

cards.q: What two ERSPAN settings are essential for a working session?
cards.a: erspan id (must match on both sides) and erspan ip-address (the destination IP); origin-ip identifies the sender.
